Kattah JC, Talkad AV, Wang DZ, Hsieh YH, Newman-Toker DE. HINTS to diagnose stroke in the acute vestibular syndrome: three-step bedside oculomotor examination more sensitive than early MRI diffusion-weighted imaging. Stroke 2009;40(11):3504–3510. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.109.551234. PMC4593511, free. Read in full; cited in 45 Syncope.

Kaufmann H, Freeman R, Biaggioni I, et al. Droxidopa for neurogenic orthostatic hypotension: a randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial (NOH301). Neurology 2014;83(4):328–335. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000000615. PMC4115605, free. Read in full; cited in 45 Syncope.

Bartalena L, Bogazzi F, Chiovato L, et al. 2018 European Thyroid Association (ETA) guidelines for the management of amiodarone-associated thyroid dysfunction. Eur Thyroid J 2018;7(2):55–66. doi:10.1159/000486957. PMC5869486, free. Read in full; cited in 98 Thyroid.

Carson JL, Terrin ML, Noveck H, et al. Liberal or restrictive transfusion in high-risk patients after hip surgery (FOCUS). N Engl J Med 2011;365(26):2453–2462. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1012452. Paywalled. Read in full; cited in 53 Hip fracture.

Neuman MD, Feng R, Carson JL, et al. Spinal anesthesia or general anesthesia for hip surgery in older adults (REGAIN). N Engl J Med 2021;385(22):2025–2035. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2113514. Paywalled; the NEJM summary slides were read, not the full paper. Cited in 53 Hip fracture.

What the syllabus mandates, against what the papers actually cite

Mandatory textbooks: Hazzard's Principles of Geriatric Medicine; the AGS Geriatrics Review Syllabus; Harrison's geriatrics chapter. Mandatory journals: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, Age and Ageing, Lancet, New England Journal of Medicine, Harefuah reviews.

Mandated sourceAppearances across the eight papers
Hazzard's~81% of every paper. The mandate and the evidence agree completely
Harrison's3–5 questions per sitting in your track. Real but small
AGS GRS30% of June 2022 and zero in every other paper
LancetDelivers — the Livingston dementia-prevention Commission reports, cited by name in 2021 and 2025
NEJMProbable but unproven: Advanced Dementia and Management of Acute Hip Fracture are both NEJM pieces and both recur, but the source tables give titles without journals
JAGSNo citation found in any of the eight papers
Age and AgeingNo citation found in any of the eight papers
Harefuah reviewsNo citation found in any of the eight papers

The mandated journal list is a weak predictor. Of the five named journals, only the Lancet clearly delivers; three produced nothing across eight sittings. Meanwhile the largest recent article cluster came from journals that are not on the list at all — JAMA Neurology supplied three questions in 2026 alone, alongside Alzheimer's & Dementia for the revised Alzheimer criteria and Diabetes Care for the ADA older-adults standards.

So do not read the mandated journals as a reading list. The pattern that actually fits eight years of papers is narrower: major consensus and criteria documents, and high-profile reviews, on a few recurring subjects — dementia diagnosis and prevention, stroke rehabilitation, hip fracture, and diabetes in older adults — wherever they happen to be published. Two of the recurring sources are not journal articles at all: the EBRSR Stroke Rehabilitation Clinician Handbook and the AGS Beers pocket guides.

Knowledge requirement beyond the 42 exam headings

The syllabus's הידע הנדרש section maps a wider content scope than the exam headings. Most of it lands under a heading that is already in the plan; a minority has no heading at all. The distinction below decides what gets reading hours.

Lands under a heading already in the plan

Syllabus content areaArrives under
Meningitis and encephalitis; tuberculosisInfections in the elderly
Sick sinus syndrome and pacemakersArrhythmia
Haematological malignanciesCancer in the elderly
White-cell, platelet and coagulation disorders; anticoagulation indications and complicationsAnemias
Tremor; peripheral neuropathy; spinal stenosisParkinson's and extrapyramidal syndromes; postural instability
Vertigo; transient loss of consciousnessFalls; postural instability
Amputation and its rehabilitation; stroke rehabilitationRehabilitation
Mechanical ventilation, short and long term, and its ethics; prolonged unconsciousnessEnd of life care; Ethics
Determination of guardianship; capacityEthics
Paget's disease and osteomalacia; myopathyOsteoporosis and osteoarthritis
Skin lesions, benign and malignant tumoursPressure sores (the syllabus's only skin heading)
Day centres, ambulatory and institutional organisation, the multidisciplinary teamGeriatrics in Israel; the geriatric team
Diverticular disease; oesophageal, gastric and duodenal diseaseConstipation; nutrition and enteral feeding

No exam heading at all

Temporal arteritis and polymyalgia rheumatica · lupus and vasculitis in the elderly · mesenteric ischaemia · interstitial lung disease · Addison's disease and corticosteroid use · valvular disease and the indications for surgery · the ischaemic or septic foot.

These get no reading hours, and the reasoning is the point. They are absent from the 42 exam headings and absent from the 46 frequency-derived topics — which means the bank's 3,833 past questions contain almost nothing on them. Two independent signals of low exam yield. Contrast the gap week: those six are named exam headings and are missing only from the bank, which is one signal of a real hole. Same evidence, opposite conclusion.

Of the seven, temporal arteritis with PMR is the one worth an hour on your own account — it is a genuine geriatric emergency you will meet at Sheba regardless of what the exam asks.

Currency, as of 12 September 2026

  • Beers 2023 is still the current edition. No 2026 update published. AGS updates every 3–4 years and the next is anticipated 2026–2027 — check once in spring 2027.
  • STOPP/START v3 is still current. There is no v4.
  • One genuinely new adjacent document: the Australian Deprescribing in Older People clinical practice guideline, MJA 2026, doi:10.5694/mja2.70174, open access, 185 recommendations across when to deprescribe, ongoing need, how, and monitoring. Excellent for practice; not what this exam is written from. Read it after the other three.

Not from these documents

The five topic sections — cancer, dementia, delirium, infections and falls — are written from standard geriatric medicine, cross-referenced to the three documents above wherever a Beers or STOPP/START criterion applies. Where a threshold is conventional rather than sourced from those papers (MoCA cut-offs, TUG seconds, long-term-care fever thresholds, G8 scoring) it is described as commonly used rather than as a citation. Verify any figure you intend to quote in an exam answer against Hazzard’s or the relevant society guideline.

The ageing-pharmacology material (volume of distribution, albumin binding, the phase I versus phase II distinction behind preferring lorazepam over diazepam), the ACB threshold of 3, and the five-step deprescribing framework come from Hazzard's and the deprescribing literature, not from the three papers above. Flagged so you know which claims have a document behind them in this file and which do not.

The named sources the papers actually cite

Every one of these appears by name in a מראה מקום table, and none of them is in Hazzard's. This is the material with no textbook behind it, which is why it is listed separately and why it is worth obtaining rather than reading around. Citations below were checked against the publisher record rather than quoted from memory; where a detail could not be confirmed it is left out rather than guessed.

Dementia — diagnosis and prevention

Lancet standing Commission, 2024 report. Livingston G, Huntley J, Liu KY, et al. Dementia prevention, intervention, and care: 2024 report of the Lancet standing Commission. Lancet 2024;404(10452):572–628. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01296-0. Obtained — 57 pages, and its Table 1, the weighted attributable fractions, is now in 57 Cognitive change. Untreated vision loss and high LDL cholesterol are the additions to the twelve from 2020, and the fourteen come to 45%. Cited by name in 2021 and 2025. Read Table 1 and the executive summary's action list; the rest is policy.

The 2020 report is the one the older papers cite: Livingston G, Huntley J, Sommerlad A, et al. Lancet 2020;396(10248):413–446. Twelve risk factors, about 40% of dementia worldwide. Know which list a stem is built on — twelve or fourteen.

Revised Alzheimer criteria, Alzheimer's Association workgroup. Jack CR Jr, Andrews JS, Beach TG, et al. Revised criteria for diagnosis and staging of Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimers Dement 2024;20(8):5143–5169. doi:10.1002/alz.13859. Biological definition, the A/T/N-derived biomarker categories including blood-based markers, and the integrated biological–clinical staging.

The dissenting position — IWG. Dubois B, Villain N, Schneider L, et al. Alzheimer disease as a clinical-biological construct: an International Working Group recommendation. JAMA Neurol 2024;81(12):1304–1311. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2024.3770. Diagnosis requires a clinical syndrome and biomarkers; biomarker-positive, cognitively normal people are at risk, not diseased. The exam has cited JAMA Neurology three times in 2026 alone, and a question that pits these two documents against each other is the obvious use of them.

Vascular cognitive impairment. The VasCog-2-WSO Criteria Consortium. Revised diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive impairment and dementia — the VasCog-2-WSO criteria. JAMA Neurol, published online 16 September 2025. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2025.3242. VCID as the umbrella term with preclinical, mild and major levels; three subtypes — ischaemic, haemorrhagic, mixed; six cognitive domains; the first revision since VasCog-1 in 2014.

Advanced dementia. Mitchell SL. Advanced dementia. N Engl J Med 2015;372(26):2533–2540. doi:10.1056/NEJMcp1412652. Free in PubMed Central. The source of the tube-feeding answer, the pneumonia and eating-problem trajectories, and the comfort-feeding alternative.

Fracture and rehabilitation

Hip fracture. Bhandari M, Swiontkowski M. Management of acute hip fracture. N Engl J Med 2017;377(21):2053–2062. doi:10.1056/NEJMcp1611090. Fracture location decides the operation; arthroplasty over internal fixation for displaced femoral-neck fractures from 65 onward. Pair it with 55 Rehabilitation and 51 Osteoporosis.

Stroke rehabilitation. Teasell R, Hussein N, et al. Stroke Rehabilitation Clinician Handbook, 2020 edition, Evidence-Based Review of Stroke Rehabilitation (EBRSR), ebrsr.com — free, and not a journal article, which is why it is easy to miss when hunting the citations. Obtained: seven chapters — clinical consequences; brain reorganisation, recovery and organised care; lower extremity; upper extremity; cognitive impairment; medical complications; depression and community reintegration. Chapters 2 and 6 are worked into 55 Rehabilitation; read chapter 2 first, because the recovery time-course numbers are the examinable part.

Diabetes

ADA Standards of Care, Section 13: Older Adults. American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 13. Older adults: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl. 1):S277–S296. doi:10.2337/dc26-S013. Obtained, and worked into 99 Diabetes. Revised every January, so cite the year you read; note that this section carries an explicit endorsement from the American Geriatrics Society. The three health-status categories and their targets, deintensification, and the geriatric syndromes section. Diabetes Care is not on the syllabus's mandatory journal list and has supplied questions anyway.

What this tells you about the mandatory journal list

The pattern that fits eight years of papers is not a journal list at all: it is major consensus and criteria documents, and high-profile clinical reviews, on a few recurring subjects — dementia diagnosis and prevention, stroke rehabilitation, hip fracture, diabetes in older adults — wherever they happen to be published. Two of the most frequently cited items are not journal articles at all: the EBRSR handbook and the AGS pocket guides. Chasing JAGS and Age and Ageing issue by issue has produced nothing in eight sittings.

Still to obtain, and the honest gaps

Three of the named sources are now in hand and worked into the sections: the Lancet 2024 Commission into 57 Cognitive change, ADA 2026 Section 13 into 99 Diabetes, and the EBRSR handbook into 55 Rehabilitation. What follows is what is still outstanding.

  • The 2020 Lancet Commission DOI is not printed here because the volume and pages were confirmed and the identifier was not. Retrieve it by title.
  • Several מראה מקום entries give a title without a journal. Advanced Dementia and Management of Acute Hip Fracture are both NEJM and both recur, which is strong but not proof that those tables mean these papers.
  • A citation carried in an earlier version of this file was wrong: the IWG recommendation was recorded as JAMA Neurol 2024;81(12):1245–1257. That page range belongs to an accompanying editorial; the paper itself is 1304–1311. Corrected above.
  • The Brookdale/JDC yearbook (קשישים בישראל — שנתון סטטיסטי) supplies one to two questions a sitting. It is free, it is updated annually, and the questions are figures — proportions over 65 and over 80, living arrangements, institutionalisation rates. Download the current edition and read the summary tables only.
  • The Israeli legal and MoH block has no document list of its own. The statutes and circulars named in the papers are set out in Ethics & EOL law; they are the most reliable four to seven questions on the paper and the ones most often left to last.
